# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

insights.line: What made the others more pressing?

whys.g1: Both answers are about the schedule slipping and subs not showing up, so one group plainly named 'The schedule and getting subs to show up' is exactly how a super would sort them.
whys.g2: There is no junk, explicit or off-topic answer on this line, so nothing junk got into the group.

founder.order_why: Screen 4 asks how far back to look for 'the last time it happened' between two context screens, before screen 5 finishes defining the moment it refers to, so the window should come after the context is complete.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 5 show the same kicker and the same question ('Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies.'), so it reads as one question asked twice.
founder.missing: The flow never asks about my solution: narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew and pushed to Procore/ACC. It never asks the price (about $1k per site per month, less for multi-site or multi-month terms). It never asks who pays: the general contractor, per site, not the superintendent who answers. Without these, my riskiest beliefs go untested: that supers will talk over videos on the walk, and that a contractor will pay $1k a site.

PRIMARY.order_why: It goes from whether my jobs are on Procore or ACC, to whether and how often I did the log this week, to what I'd want easier, to how the last log went, which is how I'd walk through it myself.
PRIMARY.missing: How long the log took me, especially the hours spent uploading the day's photos to Procore, and whether I've had to go back to old logs for something like a delay dispute with the owner.

screens.instead: Done within half an hour of the last walk · Took about an hour in the trailer · Took two or three hours · Went past three hours, into the evening · Never got written up that day

screens.why1: Just before the link goes out to supers, it's obvious why Keel asks who will put the questions to them, and by text message suits how my supers already work.
screens.why2: The question is plain, but the hint mixes 'on video' with 'the voice you pick', so I have to read it twice to know whether I'm picking a face or only a voice, and '400 credits' is Keel's word, not mine.
screens.why3: I know my supers, so I can judge from a 5-second clip which voice they'd sit through at the end of a long day in the trailer.
screens.why4: Two names with play buttons are distinct and complete, but nothing beside them says how they differ, such as accent, pace or a face, so I can't choose without playing both.
screens.why5: Nothing of Fresco or my roles leaks here, and my pick of the preselected interviewer is kept as I made it.
screens.instead: Who should ask your superintendents the questions on video? Daphne (picked for you, ▶ 5 s) or Saskia (▶ 5 s); the one you pick is recorded once for this project, 400 credits either way.

screens.why1: Once I've chosen to send interviews to supers, the next thing to settle is how they answer, so this comes in the right place before the last screen.
screens.why2: Read and tap, talk or type, and a link opened on the phone are plain to me and to supers who live on their phones in the trailer; Daphne is introduced right in the option.
screens.why3: I know how my supers work, on a phone at the end of the day, often tired and around noise, so I can pick the format from what I see them do.
screens.why4: The three choices are AI voice, text, or letting them pick; they are distinct, they cover the real choices, and each one says what the respondent actually does.
screens.why5: Nothing of Fresco's product or its buyer roles shows up here, and 'Read and tap' is what I picked.

screens.why1: After choosing who interviews and how supers answer, deciding who gets the link is the obvious last step before sending.
screens.why2: Plain words; I know exactly which supers I'd text a link to, and the Contacts page and Google sign-in are clear enough to a founder.
screens.why3: It asks about my own outreach -- the supers I met driving to Napa and the South Bay -- which I know firsthand.
screens.why4: Named people, a Keel-found list, and an open link for a group (say a superintendents' forum) are the three real ways I'd reach supers, distinct and complete.
screens.why5: My pick, people I know by name, is kept as typed and nothing of Fresco leaks to respondents here.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right under the title with 'Frequency: 4 counted' beside it, and the Frequency card shows that 5 were needed, so I know it isn't called and why.
screens.why_b2: '6 of 7 said yes · bar 6 of 7' reads at once, but '4 counted' on three cards when 7 answered makes me look again to work out why three people dropped out, and the screen never says.
screens.why_b3: Prevalence and Frequency are my beliefs, but Importance has become a clunky 'have five things that are hard... one of the two' and Current solution is reworded, though I still recognise both.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' implies I need more counted answers, but nothing tells me to get one or two more supers through, or that the log being common is already settled.
screens.why_b5: n=7 and the 4 counted are on every line, too-few is said plainly, and a prevalence that only just clears the bar at 6 of 7 is called 'holding up', not strong.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Holding up' sits right beside '6 of 7 said yes · bar 6 of 7 · at the bar', so I know it held and by exactly how much.
screens.why_b2: The strip shows 6 for and 1 against out of 7, with my bar marker at 6, readable at first look.
screens.why_b3: Prevalence is my dimension, but the belief line has become typing photos and notes into the daily log, which is the routine every super does, not the hours lost in the trailer after the walks that I counted.
screens.why_b4: The So line only points to the next two cards and says nothing about what clearing the bar means for Fresco.
screens.why_b5: The small n is named as 'a lean, not a call', but 'Holding up' rests on a gate almost any working super answers Yes to (Denise, whose log is done as she goes, counts for me), so it says more than the data shows about my problem.
screens.instead: Ask and say the costly part, 'spent time after the walks typing the log in the trailer', and then: 6 of 7 said yes, right at your 8-in-10 bar, a lean from 7 people, so check Frequency and Importance before you lean on it.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits directly beside its deciding numbers, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know where it stands and why.
screens.why_b2: Most of the chart reads at a glance: the count is working days out of 5, the middle answer is 5, and four cells are filled. But the axis starts at a 0 nobody could pick, and 'your bar · 4 of 5 (at least 2 in 3)', with its marker at 4, took me a second look to see the bar is a head count, not the 4-day low of my range.
screens.why_b3: Frequency and 'type photos and notes into the daily log on 4 to 5 working days out of 5' are my belief and my trade's words. The 'the most recent time it happened' tail on the Asked line is stray, but it doesn't change the belief.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't tell me that one more counted superintendent is all I need, or that all four counted already log on 4 or 5 days.
screens.why_b5: Nothing overclaims: the low n is said twice ('4 counted', 'a lean, not a call'), and Hank and Luis are shown as not counted with their reasons.
screens.instead: All 4 counted supers logged on 4 or 5 of the last 5 working days, with a middle answer of 5. You need one more counted answer to call it, and even if that person says fewer days, 4 of 5 still clears your bar, so this is close to holding.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know both the verdict and the number behind it.
screens.why_b2: The caption '4 people · each picked two · bars count picks (8)' and the bars are clear, and my row's 2 against 3 each for schedule and subs is plain, but 'your bar · 4 of 5' when only 4 were counted took me a second look to see it is a bar on a group of five I don't have yet.
screens.why_b3: The card says Importance, my circumstance in my words and my own row 'Typing photos and notes into the log', so I recognise it as my belief.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't tell me to get one more counted super, or that with 2 of 4 even a fifth 'for' would fall short of 4 of 5.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (6 answered, 4 counted, who was dropped and why), the low n is named as 'a lean, not a call', and nothing claims more than the four picks carry.
screens.instead: 2 of 4 supers put the log in their two, and schedule and subs drew 3 picks each. Even a fifth 'for' would make 3 of 5, under your bar of 4, so this leans against: test whether the schedule and subs, not the log, are what hurts after the walk.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', and the So line repeats both, so I know why there is no call.
screens.why_b2: The bars and the line under 'Typed up within half an hour of the walk' read at once, but the strip's '4 of 5' with a ghost cell and a marker at 4, when only 4 were counted, took me a second look to see it means the bar if a fifth person answers.
screens.why_b3: The act is my own, typing up the daily log in the trailer after the walks, and the rungs are on my measure of time after the walk, so the belief is the one I checked.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: the count line calls it 'a lean' but neither line says which way it leans (3 of 4 counted took a couple of hours or the rest of the evening) or that one more answer at an hour or worse would make it hold.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (6 answered, 4 counted, each exclusion named), the small group is called a lean and not a call, and nothing claims beyond those four.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of the 4 counted took a couple of hours or more after the walk, a lean toward your belief; one more super at 'about an hour' or worse would make it hold.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know where this stands and why.
screens.why_b3: It's my Importance belief: typing the walk's photos and notes into the daily log is one of the two hardest end-of-day jobs, and it reads as I checked it.
screens.why_b4: Nothing on the screen says what this means for Fresco; it doesn't tell me to get one more super, and it doesn't ask whether the log being deferrable weakens the pitch, and the two footer lines are about other dimensions.
screens.why_b5: The count stays visible (4 counted, 2 against, 2 asked), the low n is named, and nothing claims beyond the two quotes.
screens.why_b6: Ray's 'the log can wait till morning, the deck can't' and Denise finishing on the tablet before the gate tell me something I didn't type: the log is deferrable and the schedule and subs out-press it, which threatens my 'saves hours every evening' story.
screens.instead: Too few to call (4 of 5): one more super decides it. Both who said no put the schedule and subs ahead of the log, and one says the log can wait till morning, so test whether Fresco's pitch should lead with the schedule and crew follow-ups from the walk rather than the log.

screens.why1: It's the first screen and asks whether my jobs run on Procore or ACC before anything else, so it's obvious this is checking I'm the right guy to ask.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are the platforms I live in every day, and 'jobs you're running' is exactly how a super talks.
screens.why3: I know which platform each of my jobs is set up on without thinking about it.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it cleanly; a job on some other system or on paper is a plain No, and a gate needs no escape chip.
screens.why5: It only names the platforms my company uses and gives away nothing about whatever they're building.
screens.why6: Short and heard once; 'I'll read 2 options' is a bit stiff for a yes-or-no, where §17 says 'Yes or no.', but nothing trips me up and 'A-C-C' is said out loud on every job.

screens.why1: Right after confirming my jobs run on Procore, asking about my daily log in the last week is the obvious next thing.
screens.why2: I upload photos and type notes; nobody 'types photos', so I'd read it twice to work out whether it means the whole log entry.
screens.why3: I fill out the daily log every working day, so I know whether I did this.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it, and the two chips belong to the story box after a Yes, not to the gate.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product leaks, but the question has slid from the part that hurts, typing it all up after the walk, to the plain act of filling the log.
screens.why6: One short question followed by 'Yes or no.' is easy to hear once and answer.
screens.why7: Putting photos and notes into the daily log is what every super on a Procore job does each day, so everyone says Yes, No has nobody, and the founder's band can never be refuted, which is the card's own bad example.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you sit down after your site walks to type up the daily log? Yes / No

screens.why1: Right after I said yes to doing the daily log this week, asking how many days I did it is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: I upload or attach photos and type the notes, so 'type photos' reads a little off, but I get it on the first pass.
screens.why3: I know exactly which days this week I got the log done and which ones slid, so I can answer this from my own week.
screens.why4: One through five covers a five-day week, a yes at the gate means at least one, and 'I can't recall' fits as the out.
screens.why5: It just asks about my daily log in Procore terms, and nothing about anybody's product or plan comes through.
screens.why6: It is short, says the week once, and 'a number from 1 to 5' plus 'or say you can't recall' is easy to answer by ear.
screens.why7: Every option counts working days, there is one button per day from 1 to 5 with no zero, the unit is said once in the window phrase, the clause is 8 words, and the one escape is there; the balance depends on the founder's low, which this screen does not show.
screens.instead: On how many of the last 5 working days did you load photos and notes into the daily log? 1 · 2 · 3 · 4 · 5 · I can't recall

screens.why1: Right after asking how often I typed the day's photos and notes into the log, it makes sense to ask how that stacks up against the other after-walk work on my plate.
screens.why2: Every option is something I'd say myself (RFIs, subs, the walk, the log), and I can answer on first read.
screens.why3: These are all things I actually deal with at the end of a day on site after the walks, so I can pick from my own last day.
screens.why4: Five distinct after-walk chores in my words with no overlap, and None of these fits; RFIs lean toward the project engineer at some outfits, but plenty of supers write them too.
screens.why5: Nothing about any product or app comes through; it's just my own work listed back to me.
screens.why6: One short question, five options I can hold, and RFIs says fine out loud as letters on a job site; the RFI option is the longest but still easy to follow.
screens.why7: The own row, typing photos and notes into the log, is on the list and not first, with four other rows from the same moment, all -ing tasks on one 'made easier' measure, None of these at the first ask, and picks can land for or against.

screens.why1: After asking how often I type up the log and what I'd want easier, asking how my last one went is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: Daily log, the walk, the trailer: that's my day in my words, though saying 'daily log' twice in one breath is clunky.
screens.why3: I know exactly how long my last log took and whether it got done that night.
screens.why4: The options mix two clocks: 'within half an hour of the walk' and 'a couple of hours after the walk' are about when it got done, while 'took about an hour' and 'the rest of the evening' are about how long it took, so a slow log done right after the walk fits two; 'in the trailer' also leaves out the guys who do it on the iPad in the truck or at home.
screens.why5: Nothing of anybody's product reaches me; it's just my log and how long it ran.
screens.why6: One short question and five short options I can hold once heard, with the escape last, though 'daily log' repeats in the stem.
screens.why7: The ladder runs on time with a working rung first, a failed-outright last, five rungs in order and the escape apart, but it slides between time since the walk (rungs 1 and 3) and time spent typing (rungs 2 and 4), so the one-measure rule is bent.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. How long did it take you to type up? Under half an hour; About an hour; A couple of hours; Most of the evening; Never got done that day. Or say someone else did it.
